prayer: Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus, directing the respondents herein to allot two additional marks to the petitioner and consider her for appointment to the post of Computer Instructors Grade-I (Post Graduate cadre) under Notification No. 9/2019 dated 01.03.2019 issued by the 4th respondent.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

N. Anand Venkatesh, J.:— This writ petition has been filed for issuance of Writ of Mandamus directing the respondent to allow two additional marks to the petitioner and consider her for appointment to the post of Computer Instructors Grade-I.

2. The case of the petitioner is that she participated in the selection process initiated by the fourth respondent to fill up the post of Computer Instructors Grade-I and the petitioner was also called for a written examination. According to the petitioner, there were discrepancies in Question No. 116 and Question No. 21 and as a result of the same, even though the petitioner had give correct answers to those questions, she was not allotted marks. It is the claim of the petitioner that she has already secured 74.811 marks and if two additional marks are given to the petitioner, she will be qualified for the selection under the disability quota for B.C. Candidates.

3. Heard Ms. Lakshmi Gopinathan, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mrs. V. Annalakshmi, learned Government Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondents 1 to 3 and Mr. C. Munusamy, learned Special Government Advocate for the 4th respondents.

4. This Court had already passed an order dated 05.12.2019 in W.P. Nos. 31119 and 31121 of 2019, based on a common order dated 19.11.2019 passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court in W.P. Nos. 32343 of 2019 etc., batch, by directing to constitute an Expert Committee and the Expert Committee to consider the grievances expressed by the candidates with regard to the discrepancies found in the questions and submit a report. The facts of the present case also squarely falls within the same ambit.

5. In view of the above, the petitioner is directed to submit a representation to the Committee that has already been constituted and point out the discrepancies in Question No. 116 and Question No. 21 and the Committee shall consider the same and submit a report to the fourth respondent and the same can be considered by the fourth respondent to proceed further in the process of selection of the petitioner. The representation shall be given to the Committee by 20.12.2019 and the Committee is directed to give its report to the fourth respondent within a period of ten days thereafter.

6. This writ petition is disposed of with the above directions. There shall be no order as to costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
